skills.name: Victorian Web
skills.thesis: Ornament is value: every surface carries pattern, rule and flourish.
skills.summary: Dense ornament, engraved borders, high-contrast serif type, deep jewel colours, gold, dark wood and old paper. It recalls the 19th century and gives a page a proud, collected and gothic mood.

pack.why: A fine, thin family; use light weight and pair it with fleuron ornaments.

skills.name: Art Nouveau (web)
skills.thesis: Ornament is not decoration added to a thing: the line of the plant grows into the structure of the page.
skills.summary: Whiplash curves, plant forms and hand-drawn lettering inside framed panels. It came from Paris, Brussels, Vienna and Glasgow around 1900. On screen it suits heritage, craft and botanical brands.

pack.why: A thin, even, round-ended line that follows the flowing stroke of a plant drawing.

skills.name: De Stijl (web)
skills.thesis: Reduce form to the straight line and the primary colour, and a universal, harmonious order appears.
skills.summary: Horizontal and vertical black lines, flat fields of red, yellow and blue, and white space. It came from the Dutch group around Mondrian and Van Doesburg and reduces form to its basic parts.

pack.why: A strict, even line on a square grid with butt terminals: straight lines only, like the style itself.

use_cases: bento-like dashboards with a strong identity

skills.name: Bauhaus
skills.thesis: Form follows function, and a small kit of circle, square and triangle in three primary colours is enough to make any object for mass production.
skills.summary: Primary-colour geometry, sans-serif lower-case type and strict horizontal and vertical axes with bold diagonals. It came from the Bauhaus school in Weimar, Dessau and Berlin, and it fused craft with industrial production.

pack.why: Solid forms with square corners and no round terminal: the cut-paper geometry of the workshop.

skills.name: Constructivism (web)
skills.thesis: The page is a machine for persuasion: every element is a lever, and the diagonal gives it energy.
skills.summary: Diagonal compositions, heavy sans-serif type, photomontage and flat red, black and cream blocks. It came from the Soviet avant-garde and treats the page as a poster that makes a call to action.

pack.why: A solid, sharp-cornered family with butt terminals that reads as a stamp on a red block.

skills.name: Art Deco (web)
skills.thesis: Luxury is order: the machine age gives ornament a strict, symmetric geometry that looks rich and modern at once.
skills.summary: Symmetric geometry, stepped forms, fan and sunburst motifs and gold lines on a dark ground. It came out of the 1925 Paris exposition and stands for luxury and speed.

pack.why: A thin, even line with sharp joins that matches the gold rule and the chamfered frame.

skills.name: Mid-Century Modern
skills.thesis: Modernist form can be warm and humane when abstract shapes, natural materials and a small earth palette serve everyday life.
skills.summary: Organic and geometric shapes in mustard, teal, orange and walnut, with slab and geometric type and wide margins. It grew from Bauhaus in postwar America and Scandinavia, and it added warmth and play to modernist order.

pack.why: Solid forms with soft corners: the organic silhouette of the period, with no outline.

skills.name: Swiss International Style
skills.thesis: Design is a neutral carrier of information, and a mathematical grid makes that neutrality visible.
skills.summary: Asymmetric layouts on a mathematical grid, one neo-grotesque sans serif, flush-left text and objective photography. It came out of Zurich and Basel in the 1950s and became the default language of corporate modernism.

pack.why: A thin, even line on a strict grid with butt terminals: the icon as neutral information.

skills.name: Rams Functionalism (UI)
skills.thesis: Good design is as little design as possible: the product should be useful, understandable and honest, and then step back.
skills.summary: Quiet matt surfaces, a muted grey palette, one orange signal colour and controls that show what they do. It follows Dieter Rams and Braun and appears again in calculators, audio and phone interfaces.

pack.why: A thin, even line with a plain pictogram form, always shown with a label.

skills.name: Pop Art (web)
skills.thesis: Mass culture is the subject: the comic, the ad and the label become art when you make them big, flat and loud.
skills.summary: Flat, saturated colour, thick outlines, halftone dots and repeated mass-media images. It came from Britain and the USA in the 1950s and 1960s and treats advertising and comics as high art.

pack.why: A bold outline with a flat fill that looks like a comic panel.

skills.name: Psychedelic
skills.thesis: Design should alter perception, and a page that vibrates, flows and resists easy reading puts the viewer in an expanded state of mind.
skills.summary: Vibrating complementary colours, melting hand-drawn lettering and symmetrical swirls that fill the whole sheet. It came from San Francisco concert posters of 1966 to 1968, and it set out to reject the order of Swiss modernism.

pack.why: Heavy, swollen solid forms with no straight terminal: the weight of the poster lettering.

skills.name: Punk Zine
skills.thesis: Anyone can publish: make the page with scissors, glue and a copier, and show the seams on purpose.
skills.summary: Photocopied black and white, cut-and-paste letters, typewriter text, tape and hand scrawl. It came from the punk scenes of London and New York and shows that anyone can make a page.

pack.why: A rough, marker-like line with uneven form that reads as a hand drawing.

skills.name: Memphis Design
skills.thesis: Good taste is a convention, and a loud, cheap, playful object can carry as much meaning as a serious one.
skills.summary: Clashing primary and pastel fields, squiggles, confetti dots and black-and-white pattern on irregular geometric forms. Ettore Sottsass and the Memphis group launched it in Milan in 1981 as a joke against good taste.

pack.why: Bold forms with a hard offset tone: the flat pop geometry of the laminate.

skills.name: Grunge Editorial
skills.thesis: Legibility is not the same as communication, and a page can carry the mood of its content by looking as rough as the content feels.
skills.summary: Layered, distressed type, overprinted photographs and broken columns, set by hand in early Macintosh software. David Carson at Ray Gun and the Emigre studio made it the look of 1990s alternative music and youth magazines.

pack.why: A doubled, off-register line: the look of a bad print run.

skills.name: Y2K Aesthetic
skills.thesis: Technology is friendly and the future is shiny, so an interface should look like a new gadget that is already finished.
skills.summary: Chrome and translucent plastic, bubble shapes, silver and electric blue, and small pixel and tech type on cold gradients. It came from the dot-com boom and the first iMac in 1998, and it pictured the year 2000 as a clean, shiny future.

pack.why: Pixel-grid forms: the screen technology of the period shows in the icon.

skills.name: Japanese Dense Web
skills.thesis: Density is hospitality: show all the options at once, so the visitor never has to search.
skills.summary: Dense pages with many links, small type, bright accent colours, banners, ranking lists and tight grids. It grew from portals such as Yahoo! JAPAN and Rakuten and makes a page rich in choice.

pack.why: A compact, solid family that stays clear at 16px beside 12px to 14px text.

skills.name: Apple Aqua
skills.thesis: The screen is a liquid, tactile surface: every control is a glossy drop that invites a click.
skills.summary: Translucent blue gel buttons, pinstripe backgrounds, glossy droplets and brushed-metal windows. It came with Mac OS X in 2000 and made the screen look like water and candy.

pack.why: A solid, soft-cornered family with volume that matches the glossy, filled look of gel controls.

use_cases: app landing pages with a friendly tone

skills.name: Frutiger Aero
skills.thesis: Technology belongs to nature and the human world, so a digital interface should look clean, glossy, alive and pleasant to touch.
skills.summary: Glossy glass buttons, aqua and grass-green gradients, water, sky and bubble imagery and humanist sans type. It grew from Y2K gloss into the Windows Vista, Mac OS X Aqua and Web 2.0 look of the late 2000s.

pack.why: Soft, filled forms with round corners that sit well in a glossy round container.

skills.name: Skeuomorphism
skills.thesis: A screen control is easier to learn when it looks and behaves like a physical object that the user already knows.
skills.summary: Interfaces that copy real objects: leather, linen, wood, felt, glass and brushed metal, lit from above with gradients and layered shadows. It has roots in 1980s desktop icons and peaked in iOS 1 to 6, until iOS 7 replaced it in 2013.

pack.why: Full solid silhouettes of real objects. The container supplies the material and the light.

use_cases: games with a table or board

skills.name: Metro UI
skills.thesis: Content is the interface: remove chrome, use type and motion for hierarchy, and let flat colour tiles carry the brand.
skills.summary: Flat colour tiles, large light typography, a strict grid and content before chrome. It came from Windows Phone 7 in 2010 and drew on Swiss signage and airport wayfinding.

pack.why: A plain 2px line glyph with sharp joins that sits well inside a thin circle.

use_cases: internal tools with a clear tone

skills.name: Pixel Art Web
skills.thesis: Limits are the style: few pixels, few colours and a hard grid make a clear, playful picture.
skills.summary: Blocky sprites, a limited palette, hard pixel edges, bitmap type and game-style panels. It borrows from 8-bit and 16-bit games and makes a page feel like a game screen.

pack.why: A pixel family drawn on a strict 24px grid that fits bitmap type.

skills.name: Bohemian Web
skills.thesis: The page is a lived-in, free-spirited space: natural, layered and warm.
skills.summary: Earth tones, hand-drawn florals, macramé and woven patterns, arched shapes, warm photography and relaxed script type. It shows a free-spirited, natural and craft-based taste.

pack.why: A soft, rounded family with a two-tone fill that suits warm, crafted layouts.

skills.name: Flat Design
skills.thesis: A digital interface is honest when it shows itself as pixels and type, and does not imitate physical objects.
skills.summary: Interfaces of solid colour fields, simple geometric shapes, bold sans-serif type and no gradients or shadows. It followed Microsoft Metro in 2010 and Windows 8 in 2012, and became the default after iOS 7 in 2013.

pack.why: Solid glyphs with no depth and no detail: the form alone carries the meaning.

skills.name: Vaporwave
skills.thesis: Nostalgia for a future that did not happen: use the dead gloss of 1990s corporate culture to question it.
skills.summary: Pink and cyan gradients, Greek busts, palm trees, Japanese text, 1990s desktop windows and a sunset grid. It came from online music scenes around 2011 and looks at 1980s and 1990s consumer dreams with irony.

pack.why: A pixel family from the era of the first desktop windows, with square terminals.

skills.name: Synthwave Web
skills.thesis: The 1980s as a dream: neon, chrome and a road to the horizon.
skills.summary: A neon sunset, a perspective grid, chrome type, pink and cyan on deep violet, and scanlines. It recalls the 1980s as film and games sold it, and it feels like a night drive.

pack.why: A smooth 2px line that takes a neon glow well.

skills.name: Brutalist Web (2014)
skills.thesis: A page is a document, not a product: show the raw structure and the web serves the reader without decoration.
skills.summary: Browser-default type, blue underlined links, grey or white ground, no polish and visible structure. It came from the 2014 Brutalist Websites collection and answers the smooth, templated web.

pack.why: A thin square line with butt terminals; the thinnest family that still reads as a plain pictogram.

skills.name: Material Design
skills.thesis: Digital surfaces behave like sheets of paper with thickness and shadow, so that depth and motion explain the hierarchy of the interface.
skills.summary: A system of flat coloured surfaces that sit at defined elevations and cast shadows from a top-left key light, with bold colour, an 8dp grid and purposeful motion. Google announced it at I/O in June 2014.

pack.why: The filled system set of the style itself, on its 24dp grid.

skills.name: Conceptual Sketch UI
skills.thesis: The page shows thinking: a rough line says the idea is open and honest.
skills.summary: Pencil and ink lines, rough outlines, margin notes, arrows and annotations on a pale ground. It shows an idea before it is finished, and feels like a designer's notebook.

pack.why: A hand-drawn line family with a slight wobble that matches pencil lines.

skills.name: Wabi-Sabi Web
skills.thesis: Imperfection is beauty: a worn, quiet surface shows time and honest craft.
skills.summary: Muted earth tones, rough textures, uneven edges, much quiet space and small, calm type. It finds beauty in what is imperfect, old and incomplete, and it is the slow side of minimal design.

pack.why: A fine, calm line that adds little weight to a quiet page.

skills.name: Anti-Design
skills.thesis: Polish is a lie: a page that breaks the rules on purpose shows that people made it.
skills.summary: Broken grids, clashing type, overlap, odd colour and deliberate roughness. It answers the polish of templated product sites and asks the visitor to notice the design.

pack.why: A loud, thick, slightly rough line that suits cut-out and sticker art.

skills.name: Dark-Mode Developer Tool
skills.thesis: A tool for experts is a dense, calm, dark instrument: show a lot, keep it quiet and make everything reachable from the keyboard.
skills.summary: Near-black surfaces, 1px hairline borders, one saturated accent, a monospace for data and keyboard hints on every action. It came from code editors and terminals and now defines software for engineers.

pack.why: A thin, even 1.5px line at 16px that sits beside 13px text without weight.

skills.name: Corporate Memphis
skills.thesis: Friendly, abstract people with unreal bodies make a corporate product feel human and inclusive without the risk of a specific face.
skills.summary: Flat vector illustrations of people with oversized limbs and tiny heads, drawn in a bright palette of 4 to 6 hues with no outlines. Facebook's Alegria system set it in 2017, and many software firms copied it.

pack.why: A friendly round line with one flat tint: the same two-tone logic as the illustrations.

skills.name: Terminal / TUI Web
skills.thesis: The terminal is the honest interface: a fixed character grid, text only and a keyboard make a tool fast and trustworthy.
skills.summary: A monospace grid, box-drawing borders, a dark or phosphor ground and keyboard hints. It borrows from command-line tools and text user interfaces to make web pages that feel like a terminal.

pack.why: A pixel family made on a strict square grid that fits a character-cell page.

skills.name: Aurora Gradient UI
skills.thesis: Colour is atmosphere: a blurred field of light makes a product feel alive without any picture of it.
skills.summary: Soft, blurred mesh gradients in 3 to 5 hues behind clean sans-serif type, with glowing edges and grain. It came from fintech and AI product pages and replaced the flat hero.

pack.why: A thin, round line that stays light on a glowing, blurred ground.

skills.name: Scrapbook UI
skills.thesis: The page is a handmade album: warm, imperfect and made by a person.
skills.summary: Cut-out photos, tape, stickers, torn paper, handwritten notes and slight tilts on a paper ground. It makes a page feel like a handmade album and a personal object.

pack.why: A hand-drawn, sticker-like family with a thick round line.

skills.name: Neumorphism
skills.thesis: An interface can be tactile without imitating objects, if every control is moulded from the same material as the page behind it.
skills.summary: Monochrome surfaces that look extruded from or pressed into the background, made with a light shadow and a dark shadow on opposite corners. It appeared on Dribbble in late 2019 as a soft answer to flat design.

pack.why: A thin round line that does not compete with the soft relief of the surface.

skills.name: Cybercore Web
skills.thesis: The page is a machine interface: sharp, labelled, cold and dense with data.
skills.summary: Black grounds, acid-green or cyan accents, chrome, angular cuts, HUD frames, small caps data labels and glitch. It mixes 1990s cyber fiction with techwear, and it feels like a machine interface.

pack.why: A technical, square-cap line family that matches clipped panels and HUD labels.

skills.name: Glassmorphism
skills.thesis: Layers are readable when each one is a pane of frosted glass: it shows what lies beneath it and still keeps its own plane.
skills.summary: Translucent panels that blur the colourful shapes behind them, edged with a thin light border. It spread after macOS Big Sur in 2020 and revives the glass of Frutiger Aero with real backdrop blur.

pack.why: A light round line that stays legible on a blurred, bright surface.

skills.name: Neo-Brutalism UI
skills.thesis: An interface earns trust by showing its structure openly and being loud about it, because every border and shadow is a stated fact.
skills.summary: Flat, loud colour fields with thick black borders and hard, unblurred offset shadows. It grew from product sites such as Gumroad and from Figma community kits as a deliberate reply to corporate softness.

pack.why: A heavy line with a blunt weight that matches the thick borders.

skills.name: Claymorphism
skills.thesis: The interface is a toy: soft, inflated forms with colour make the screen friendly and touchable.
skills.summary: Puffy, rounded 3D shapes in soft pastel colour with double inner shadows and a soft outer shadow, like modelling clay. It followed neumorphism and flat illustration and turns the interface into toys.

pack.why: A bold, round, filled family that looks inflated, like clay, inside a pastel disc.

use_cases: consumer wellness and finance for young users

skills.name: Editorial Serif Revival
skills.thesis: Voice beats neutrality: a serif with character makes a brand sound like a person, as in a magazine.
skills.summary: Large expressive serif headlines, warm off-white paper, a small sans for labels and a restrained palette. It came back as a reaction to the geometric sans-serif default of the SaaS web.

pack.why: A thin, even, humanist line that does not compete with the serif headlines.

skills.name: Ethereal Web
skills.thesis: Lightness is luxury: haze, glow and space make a quiet, weightless world.
skills.summary: Pale, glowing pastels, soft focus, thin serif or light sans type, translucent layers and air. It aims at a calm, dreamlike, weightless mood and reads as light rather than as object.

pack.why: A fine round line; set the weight to light so icons stay quiet.

skills.name: AI Chat Interface
skills.thesis: The interface is a conversation: one box to speak into, and everything else appears in the reply.
skills.summary: A single centred column, one large input at the bottom, streaming text, suggestion chips and almost no chrome. It came with ChatGPT in 2022 and makes language the main control.

pack.why: A thin, neutral 1.5px line at 16px to 20px that stays quiet next to running text.

skills.name: Bento Grid UI
skills.thesis: A page is easiest to scan when every idea sits in its own compartment and the compartments tile one tight, regular grid.
skills.summary: A rectangular grid of rounded cells of mixed spans, each holding one idea, with equal small gaps between them. Apple feature pages made it the default product layout from 2022.

pack.why: A plain round line at one weight: quiet in a cell, the default of current product interfaces.

skills.name: Spatial UI (visionOS)
skills.thesis: An interface in space should be a physical presence in the room, so it uses glass that takes light from the real scene and respects the person's field of view.
skills.summary: Translucent glass windows that float in the user's room at a set distance, lit by the surrounding scene and controlled by eye gaze and hand pinch. Apple introduced it with Vision Pro in 2023.

pack.why: Thin, round system glyphs in the platform manner, made for a round glass container.

use_cases: web marketing pages for spatial devices

skills.name: Liquid Glass
skills.thesis: Controls are a transparent lens above the content: the interface floats, refracts the page and stays out of the way.
skills.summary: Clear, curved glass that bends the content behind it, with specular edges, tint that adapts to the ground and floating controls. Apple introduced it in 2025 and it goes beyond frosted glass.

pack.why: An iOS-style family with round forms and a medium weight that matches a system sans on glass.

skills.name: Art Nouveau
skills.thesis: A building should grow like a plant: structure, ornament and furniture follow one organic line, and iron and glass are shown as the new materials of the age.
skills.summary: Whiplash curves, plant forms and exposed iron on the street front and in the stair hall. Horta in Brussels, Guimard in Paris and Gaudí in Barcelona made the total work of art: one line from the facade to the door handle.

skills.name: Bauhaus Architecture
skills.thesis: Form follows use: each function gets its own volume, and the plan is the generator of the building, not the facade.
skills.summary: A functional building of asymmetric wings, each wing sized by its use, joined by bridges and glazed on the work side. Gropius and Meyer taught building as the last step of a workshop education that joined art, craft and industry.

skills.name: Art Deco
skills.thesis: Modern technology deserves luxury: the machine age should look glamorous, symmetric and expensive.
skills.summary: Stepped towers, zigzag and chevron relief, and rich materials in a symmetric frame. It came from the Paris exhibition of 1925 and made the skyscraper and the cinema into the pictures of the machine age.

skills.name: International Style
skills.thesis: A building is a volume enclosed by a thin skin, and industrial methods make one rational form valid in every place.
skills.summary: Light rectilinear volumes of steel, glass and white render, with flat roofs, ribbon windows and free plans. The Bauhaus, Le Corbusier and Mies van der Rohe defined it in the 1920s, and it became the global language of the office tower.

skills.name: Mid-century Modern
skills.thesis: Modern architecture can be warm: the free plan and the glass wall serve everyday life, and the house belongs to its garden.
skills.summary: A low house of post-and-beam timber or steel, with glass walls to the garden, a flat or low-pitched roof and a warm palette. It made the International Style domestic and suited it to climate, family and the car.

skills.name: Brutalism
skills.thesis: A building is honest when its material, its structure and its use are legible from the street.
skills.summary: Heavy masses of board-marked concrete with the structure, the services and the circulation shown on the outside. It grew from Le Corbusier's late work and from British post-war housing, and it built the universities and town halls of the welfare state.

skills.name: Postmodernism
skills.thesis: Architecture is communication: a building should carry meaning, memory and irony, and a decorated shed is better than a blank box.
skills.summary: A building that quotes history in a joke and in colour: split pediments, giant keystones, pastel stone and a facade that works as a sign. Venturi, Graves and Johnson used it to answer the blank box of the Modern Movement.

skills.name: High-tech
skills.thesis: A building is a machine of parts: structure, services and circulation are tools to see and to change, and open floors let the use change.
skills.summary: A lightweight steel frame, with the services, the bracing and the lifts shown in colour on the outside. Rogers, Piano and Foster made the machine aesthetic of the 1920s into a flexible, kit-of-parts building.

skills.name: Deconstructivism
skills.thesis: The pure form is already flawed: distort the grid, collide the volumes and let the building show that order is unstable.
skills.summary: Skewed, fractured volumes that collide at sharp angles, with a facade that seems to tear itself apart. Gehry, Hadid, Libeskind and Coop Himmelb(l)au used distortion to disturb the pure box of the Modern Movement from inside.

skills.name: Georgian
skills.thesis: A room is good when its proportions obey the classical rules and each wall answers the wall opposite it.
skills.summary: The British and colonial room of the four Georges. Walls follow a classical order of dado, field and cornice; a chimneypiece on the centre line, paired doors and sash windows set one axis; mahogany furniture stands against the walls, and the centre of the floor stays clear.

skills.name: Shaker
skills.thesis: A room is beautiful when each object in it is useful, well made and in its place.
skills.summary: The rooms of the United Society of Believers in Christ's Second Appearing in New England, New York and Kentucky. Built-in storage, a peg rail around the walls, light wood furniture and bare floor give a room that is ordered for work and easy to clean.

skills.name: Victorian
skills.thesis: A home shows the taste, the travels and the respectability of its family; more objects and more pattern mean more comfort.
skills.summary: The middle-class room of the industrial century. Machine-made pattern covers walls, floors and furniture; dark, saturated colours, heavy curtains and many objects make a dense, enclosed parlour around the hearth.

skills.name: Arts and Crafts
skills.thesis: A room is honest when every piece is made by hand from local materials and shows how it is made.
skills.summary: The craft reform of the Victorian room. Handmade oak furniture shows its joints, a deep inglenook holds the hearth, and one stylised plant pattern runs on the walls or the textiles; low beams and built-in settles make the room honest and warm.

skills.name: Art Nouveau
skills.thesis: Nature gives the only true line; one designer must draw every part of a room so that it grows as one plant.
skills.summary: The room as one living organism. Whiplash curves of plant stems run from the furniture into the panelling, the door frames and the light fittings; stained glass, carved fruitwood and bronze make each room a total work of art by one designer.

skills.name: Bauhaus interior
skills.thesis: A room is a machine for daily life, and industry can make each of its parts well and for everyone.
skills.summary: The rooms that the Bauhaus workshops in Weimar and Dessau designed and furnished. Tubular steel, glass, lacquer and woven wool stand in white rooms with one primary-colour wall; each object is a prototype for industry, and the room is a tool for living.

skills.name: Art Deco
skills.thesis: Luxury and the machine meet in one bold geometric order of rare materials and high contrast.
skills.summary: The luxury room of the machine age. Symmetric plans, stepped and fan geometry, black lacquer, exotic veneers and polished chrome or brass give high contrast; a mirror or a mural on the axis and cove light in the ceiling make the room a stage.

skills.name: Hollywood Regency
skills.thesis: A room is a stage set: bold colour, gloss and symmetry make the people in it look their best.
skills.summary: The decorator's room of the film stars. Regency and neoclassical forms meet lacquer colour, bold stripes and mirror; a symmetric plan around a centre piece, white plaster and gilt make each room ready for a camera.

skills.name: Mid-century modern interior
skills.thesis: The modern home joins the room to the landscape, and good design made in series can be warm as well as rational.
skills.summary: The open-plan post-war home of the United States and Europe. Low teak and moulded-plywood furniture on tapered legs stands in front of a glass wall to the garden; a stone fireplace or the view is the focal point, and a few saturated accents warm a neutral room.

skills.name: Scandinavian interior
skills.thesis: A home for a long dark winter must be bright, warm in material and made of few good things that last.
skills.summary: The bright, light-wood room of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland. White walls and pale floors catch the short northern daylight; solid-wood furniture with visible joints and wool textiles stand in small groups, and many small lamps replace one ceiling light.

skills.name: Industrial loft
skills.thesis: The building tells of its past as a factory; leave the structure and the services in view and live among them.
skills.summary: The converted factory floor. Exposed brick, concrete, steel columns and ducts stay in view; large steel windows light one open plan, and salvaged furniture of wood, leather and steel stands in zones on a bare floor.

skills.name: Memphis interior
skills.thesis: Function is not the only meaning of an object; colour, pattern and irony are functions too.
skills.summary: The rooms of the Milan design group around Ettore Sottsass. Furniture is a stack of primary solids in plastic laminate, printed with squiggles and terrazzo chips in clashing colours; each piece stands alone like a sculpture, and no axis or rule of good taste orders the room.

skills.name: Minimalist
skills.thesis: Remove every thing that is not necessary, so that space, light and material can be seen.
skills.summary: The room reduced to space, light and surface. White or pale stone walls, one floor material throughout, hidden storage and flush details leave only one or two pieces in view; daylight on a plain wall is the main event.
use_cases: homes of collectors of one object

skills.name: Japandi
skills.thesis: Calm comes from emptiness and from a few natural things made by hand and placed with care.
skills.summary: A blend of the Scandinavian room and the Japanese room. Low, heavy wood furniture in pale and dark tones stands in a warm off-white room with wide empty floor; paper light, linen, stoneware and slatted screens give texture, and the tatami ratio of 1:2 orders the plan.

skills.name: Grandmillennial
skills.thesis: Comfort and memory beat the cool, empty room: inherited, pretty and patterned things make a home.
skills.summary: A young generation takes back the rooms of its grandparents. Chintz, ruffles, needlepoint, skirted tables, wicker and blue-and-white porcelain return with a fresh, light palette and a sense of humour; pattern meets pattern and inherited pieces meet new ones.

skills.name: Neo-deco
skills.thesis: Deco glamour without the hard edges: curves, ribs and warm metal make luxury feel soft and personal.
skills.summary: Art Deco after a century, made soft. Curved bouclé and velvet seats, fluted wood, arches, ribbed glass and brushed brass keep the geometry and the glamour of the 1920s, but in warm, muted colours and rounded forms.

skills.name: Dopamine decor
skills.thesis: Colour and play in the home lift the mood, and a room must show the joy of the person who lives in it.
skills.summary: A room built for joy after the years at home of 2020 and 2021. Saturated hues drench walls, trim and ceiling; curved, inflated furniture in velvet and bouclé stands on patterned rugs; objects are personal and sorted by colour.

skills.name: Quiet luxury
skills.thesis: Real luxury is the quality of the material and the work, and it does not need to show a name.
skills.summary: A tonal room of costly materials and no logos. One hue family in cream, oatmeal, taupe and chocolate covers walls and seats; texture, not colour, gives the variety; pairs of chairs and lamps mirror about the fireplace, and hidden light washes the plaster.

skills.name: Pictorialism
skills.thesis: A photograph is art when the maker's hand shows in the image, so the print must look made and not recorded.
skills.summary: Photography that borrows the look of drawing and etching. Soft-focus lenses, hand-worked pigment prints and warm toning blur the line between a photograph and a painting, to claim the status of art.

skills.name: Straight photography
skills.thesis: Photography is an art of its own when it shows the world with the full detail and tonal range that only a camera can record.
skills.summary: A sharp, unmanipulated print of a real thing, made on a large camera at a small aperture. The beauty comes from the medium itself: fine detail, a long tonal scale and exact focus from front to back.

skills.name: Street photography
skills.thesis: Public life holds pictures that nobody can stage, and the photographer's job is to be in the right place and to see them in time.
skills.summary: Unposed pictures of public life, made with a small camera, a wide lens and quick reflexes. The photographer finds the frame and waits for the moment when gesture, light and geometry agree.
use_cases: campaign imagery with a raw feel

skills.name: New Colour
skills.thesis: Colour is the subject and not a decoration, and the everyday world is rich enough to need no drama.
skills.summary: Colour photography of the plain American scene: a car park, a kitchen, a tricycle. Saturated dye-transfer and slide colour carries the picture, and the composition looks casual and exact at the same time.

skills.name: New Topographics
skills.thesis: The ordinary, man-made landscape deserves the formal care that the sublime wilderness once received, and the photographer's voice should stay out of it.
skills.summary: Flat, neutral, frontal views of suburbs, car parks and industrial sites, with no drama and no opinion. It shows the built landscape as a catalogue of facts, in a cool, exact, almost clerical style.

skills.name: Y2K digicam
skills.thesis: The flaws of a cheap early sensor are the style: they mark a moment in time and read as honest.
skills.summary: The look of a 2 to 5 megapixel CCD compact: deep focus from a tiny sensor, blown highlights, a hard on-camera flash, over-sharpened edges and clumsy white balance. It is a record of a device and now a deliberate nostalgia.
use_cases: fashion and music campaigns with a nostalgic tone

skills.name: Cinematic teal and orange
skills.thesis: Two opposed hues, the warm skin and the cool environment, give a frame instant depth and a sense of cinema.
skills.summary: A staged, shallow-focus frame with warm orange skin against cool teal shadows, graded like a film still. It is a colour recipe from the digital intermediate, and it is now a default look of films, ads and image prompts.

skills.name: Party flash
skills.thesis: The harsh direct flash is the honest light of a real night, and an image that looks unplanned and unflattering reads as truthful and as cool.
skills.summary: A night-out picture lit by one hard flash on the camera. The subject glows against a falling-off, dark background, skin shines and colour is bold; the image looks candid, tipsy and slightly rude.

skills.name: German Expressionist cinema
skills.thesis: The set, the light and the body show inner fear, so the picture is built as a state of mind and not recorded as a place.
skills.summary: A studio cinema of painted sets, hard single-source light and distorted perspective. The frame shows the mind of the character, not the street. Black-and-white prints are tinted by scene.
use_cases: horror and thriller titles and trailers
music video with a gothic set
video prompts for a haunted or dream scene

skills.name: Soviet montage
skills.thesis: Meaning comes from the collision of shots, not from the content of a single shot, so the edit is the author of the film.
skills.summary: A cinema made in the cutting room. Two shots meet and a third meaning appears. Fast cuts, steep angles and typed faces drive the argument of the film.
use_cases: music video with a hard rhythm
brand film about industry or labour

skills.name: French New Wave
skills.thesis: A film is a personal essay shot on location with light gear, so the director's eye and the street replace the studio and the script department.
skills.summary: Light 35mm cameras, fast black-and-white stock and real streets. A handheld camera, a jump cut and a director who shows the hand. The film talks about film.
use_cases: video prompts for a city walk

skills.name: Dogme 95
skills.thesis: A fixed set of prohibitions removes illusion, polish and the director's taste, so that the truth of the scene remains.
skills.summary: A film made under a written vow: handheld camera, real locations, available light and the sound of the scene. The rules remove the tools that fake the world, so the actors and the room carry the film.
use_cases: video prompts for a raw family scene

skills.name: Creator vlog
skills.thesis: A direct address from one person, tightened by the jump cut, builds more trust than a produced film, so the creator's pace is the style.
skills.summary: A person talks to the lens in a room or on the move. Every pause is cut out, and a title, a sound or a cut-away lands every few seconds. The creator is the set, the brand and the grade.
use_cases: video prompts for a day-in-the-life clip

skills.name: Vertical short-form
skills.thesis: A viewer swipes in 1 to 2 s, so every second must earn the next: the hook, the cut and the caption are the whole design.
skills.summary: A full-screen 9:16 clip of 15 to 45 s, shot on a phone and cut every 1.5 to 3 s. A hook in the first second, burned-in captions and a sound that can loop. The feed decides each rule.
use_cases: video prompts for a vertical clip

skills.name: Cinematic FPV
skills.thesis: A camera that can go anywhere should not cut: one unbroken flight turns space itself into the story.
skills.summary: One continuous flight through a place: a small drone with an ultra-wide camera dives, banks and threads gaps at 15 to 35 m/s. The camera moves like a bird, and the cut hides inside a wipe.
use_cases: music video with a one-take flight
video prompts for a drone fly-through

skills.name: Camcorder revival
skills.thesis: A flawed, low-resolution tape image looks like a real memory, so the defect is the proof of the moment.
skills.summary: A 4:3 picture with tape noise, a date stamp and a shaky hand. It looks like a home video from 1985 to 2005. Creators shoot on old Hi8 and MiniDV or add the look in post, to look near and unpolished.
use_cases: video prompts for a memory or a party

skills.name: Renaissance painting
skills.thesis: A picture is a window onto a measured space, and the ideal human body is the measure of that space.
skills.summary: A picture as a measured window onto the world: linear perspective, modelled figures, a stable geometry and a calm, idealised body. Florentine and Venetian workshops and Flemish oil painters set the rules.

skills.name: Baroque painting
skills.thesis: A picture is a staged moment in which light decides what matters and the viewer feels the event.
skills.summary: Painting of the instant: strong chiaroscuro, diagonal movement, warm earth colour and a viewer who is pulled into the scene. It serves the church, the court and the new Dutch market for portraits and domestic life.

skills.name: Ukiyo-e
skills.thesis: A picture is a printed sheet in which the contour, the flat colour and the cropped viewpoint carry everything, and the moment is as fleeting as the city.
skills.summary: Japanese woodblock prints and paintings of the Edo city: a firm black contour, flat fields of colour, bold cropping and a high or tilted viewpoint. A team of artist, carver and printer makes each sheet, and publishers sell it to a mass market.

skills.name: Impressionism
skills.thesis: A picture records the impression of light on a surface at one moment, not the object as it is known to be.
skills.summary: Painting of the first look: quick, broken strokes of pure colour that record changing light on a modern scene. The painters work outdoors, drop the outline and the black shadow, and let the viewer's eye mix the colour.

skills.name: Nordic national romanticism
skills.thesis: A picture can give a young nation a face by painting its own land, light, legends and home with the best methods of Europe.
skills.summary: Painting that builds a nation's image from its own land, myths and home life: pale northern light, lake and forest, folk legend and the farm room. Painters trained in Paris bring back plein-air method and apply it to Nordic subjects.
use_cases: Nordic heritage and tourism art direction
book illustration for myth and legend

skills.name: Cubism
skills.thesis: A picture is an object in its own right, and it shows what a thing is by combining several viewpoints on one flat surface.
skills.summary: A picture that shows an object from several sides at once. Analytic Cubism breaks the subject into faceted planes in a narrow brown-grey key; Synthetic Cubism rebuilds it from flat shapes, pasted paper and brighter colour.
use_cases: portrait illustration with a modern edge

skills.name: De Stijl painting
skills.thesis: A picture shows universal order when it uses only the horizontal and the vertical, the three primaries and the three non-colours, balanced without symmetry.
skills.summary: A picture reduced to straight black lines, rectangles of primary colour and white or grey, in asymmetric balance. Mondrian and van Doesburg wanted a universal language of pure relations that could also order a room or a city.

skills.name: Abstract Expressionism
skills.thesis: A painting is the record of an act, and its scale, its marks and its colour put the viewer inside the feeling and not in front of an image.
skills.summary: Large abstract paintings in which the act of painting is the subject: gesture, drip and slash in one camp, large soft fields of colour in the other. The canvas is an arena for an event, and it is big enough to surround the viewer.
